name: יַאֲזַנְיָהוּ
summary: Four men of the last days of Judah: Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, a captain who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah (2Ki 25:23), spelled יְזַנְיָהוּ in Jer 40:8 and called son of Hoshaiah in Jer 42:1; Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, a Rechabite whom Jeremiah tested with wine (Jer 35:3); Jaazaniah son of Shaphan, standing among the seventy elders who burned incense to idols in the chambers of the temple (Ezk 8:11); and Jaazaniah son of Azzur, a prince of the people who gave wicked counsel in the city (Ezk 11:1–2). The name is the imperfect of the hiphil הֶאֱזִין with יָהוּ: “Yahweh gives ear”, what the psalmist asks and finds (Psa 77:2). Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “וְיַאֲזַנְיָהוּ son of the Maacathite, they and their men.”
“וִיזַנְיָה son of Hoshaiah”, among the captains.
“I took יַאֲזַנְיָה son of Jeremiah … and all the house of the Rechabites.”
“וְיַאֲזַנְיָהוּ son of Shaphan standing in their midst”, each with his censer.
“יַאֲזַנְיָה son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, princes of the people … who devise iniquity.”
“My voice to God, and he gave ear (וְהַאֲזִין) to me”: the verb of the name.

note: Takes a.cg.ai (6 tokens, both spellings) and the zero-token cross-references j.ac.ac (יַאֲזַנְיָה) and j.bc.ad (יְזַנְיָה). TIPNR files the Maacathite of 2Ki 25:23 and Jer 40:8 together with the son of Hoshaiah of Jer 42:1 (and Azariah, Jer 43:2) as Jezaniah@2Ki.25.23. The reading 'Yahweh gives ear' takes יַאֲזַנְ‑ as a hiphil imperfect of אָזַן; no verse gives the meaning.
